questions.q: Photochemical smog contains which harmful secondary pollutant?
questions.exp: PAN and ozone are formed by sunlight acting on hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides.

questions.q: The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to limit the global average temperature rise to
options: Well below 2 °C above pre-industrial levels, pursuing 1.5 °C
questions.exp: The Paris Agreement under UNFCCC seeks to hold warming well below 2 °C and pursue 1.5 °C.

questions.q: Which statutory body at the national level is headed by the Prime Minister under the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
questions.exp: NDMA, established under the 2005 Act, has the Prime Minister as chairperson.

questions.q: The 3 R's principle of waste management stands for
questions.exp: The 3 R's - reduce, reuse and recycle - form the basic waste hierarchy.

questions.q: The Chipko Movement, which involved hugging trees to prevent felling, began in the 1970s in which present-day state?
questions.exp: Chipko began in Chamoli district (now Uttarakhand); Sunderlal Bahuguna and Gaura Devi are associated with it.

questions.q: The Silent Valley movement in Kerala was launched to oppose
options: A hydroelectric project on the Kunthipuzha river
A mining project in the Western Ghats
A highway through a tiger reserve
questions.exp: The protest saved the Silent Valley rainforest and led to a National Park (1985).

questions.q: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by the UN in 2015 for achievement by 2030?
questions.exp: The 2030 Agenda adopted 17 SDGs with 169 targets; the Millennium Development Goals were eight.

questions.q: El Niño is characterised by
options: Warming of the Arctic Ocean only
Abnormal warming of surface water in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean
questions.exp: El Niño often weakens the Indian summer monsoon.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a method of in-situ conservation?
questions.exp: A seed bank stores seeds outside the natural habitat and is therefore ex-situ.

questions.q: The intensity or magnitude of an earthquake is recorded by which instrument?
questions.exp: A seismograph records ground vibrations; magnitude is expressed on the Richter scale.

questions.q: The Chernobyl accident of 1986 was a major case of
questions.exp: A nuclear reactor explosion released radioactive isotopes over large areas of Europe.

questions.q: Which of the following pollutants is mainly responsible for acid rain?
options: Sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen
questions.exp: SO2 and NOx form sulphuric and nitric acids, lowering rain pH below 5.6.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-renewable source of energy?
questions.exp: Natural gas is a fossil fuel formed over millions of years and cannot be replenished quickly.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT biodegradable?
questions.exp: Plastics such as polythene are not broken down by microbes in a reasonable time.

questions.q:
Statement I: A population growing in an unlimited-resource environment shows a J-shaped curve.
Statement II: Logistic growth in a limited environment shows an S-shaped curve.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.exp: Exponential growth gives a J-curve; limited resources lead to logistic S-curve with carrying capacity K.

questions.q: The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora is commonly known as
questions.exp: CITES (1973, Washington) regulates international trade in endangered species.

questions.q: Which of the following is an ex-situ method of conserving biodiversity?
questions.exp: Ex-situ conservation protects species outside their natural habitat, e.g. zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks.

questions.q: Free-living nitrogen-fixing bacteria in soil include
questions.exp: Azotobacter fixes nitrogen without a host; Rhizobium lives symbiotically in legume root nodules.

questions.q: The plant Cuscuta (dodder) growing on a host plant is an example of
questions.exp: Cuscuta is a parasitic climber that draws nutrients from its host.

questions.q: Which of the following is the first step in the disaster management cycle aimed at reducing the impact of a future disaster?
questions.exp: Mitigation and preparedness precede response and recovery measures.

questions.q: Landslides in hilly areas are mainly aggravated by
questions.exp: Removal of vegetation loosens soil, which slides down during heavy rain.

questions.q: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was passed in India in
questions.exp: The Water Act was passed in 1974; the Air Act followed in 1981.

questions.q: Organic farming mainly avoids the use of
questions.exp: Organic farming relies on compost, manure and biological pest control.

questions.q: Rainwater harvesting is mainly done to
questions.exp: Collecting and storing rainwater helps recharge aquifers and reduces dependence on groundwater.

questions.q: E-waste mainly consists of
questions.exp: E-waste includes computers, phones and appliances, often containing lead, mercury and cadmium.

questions.q:
Statement I: Carbon dioxide is the main gas responsible for enhanced global warming due to human activities.
Statement II: Burning of fossil fuels and deforestation increase atmospheric CO2.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.exp: Fossil fuel burning and deforestation raise CO2, the largest contributor to anthropogenic warming.

questions.q: A major difference between a National Park and a Wildlife Sanctuary is that in a National Park
options: Private ownership of land is encouraged
Human activities such as grazing and forestry are not permitted
questions.exp: National parks have stricter protection with no grazing or collection of forest produce.

questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable resource?
questions.exp: Forests regenerate if managed sustainably, unlike fossil fuels.

questions.q: The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan is well known for protecting
questions.exp: In 1730 Amrita Devi and villagers of Khejarli died trying to save khejri trees.

questions.q: Minamata disease, first reported in Japan, is caused by poisoning from
questions.exp: Methylmercury released in industrial waste accumulated in fish eaten by local people.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an energy source obtained from Earth's internal heat?
questions.exp: Geothermal energy uses heat from within Earth, e.g. hot springs and steam.

questions.q: Decomposers such as fungi and bacteria play an important role in an ecosystem by
options: Recycling nutrients from dead organic matter
questions.exp: Decomposers break down dead matter, returning mineral nutrients to the soil.

questions.q: Biomagnification refers to the
options: Decrease in energy at higher trophic levels
Increase in concentration of a non-degradable toxin at successive trophic levels
questions.exp: Substances such as DDT and mercury accumulate and are present in higher concentration at higher trophic levels.

questions.q: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary in Bihar protects which aquatic mammal?
questions.exp: The sanctuary along the Ganga near Bhagalpur protects the Ganges river dolphin, India's national aquatic animal.

questions.q: A species found only in a particular geographical area and nowhere else is called
questions.exp: Endemic species are restricted to a specific region, e.g. lion-tailed macaque of the Western Ghats.

questions.q: In an ecosystem, the pyramid of energy is always
questions.exp: Energy decreases at each trophic level, so the energy pyramid cannot be inverted.

questions.q: The first species to colonise bare rock in primary succession are usually
questions.exp: Crustose lichens secrete acids that weather rock and start soil formation.

questions.q: The Bhopal gas tragedy of December 1984 was caused by the leakage of
questions.exp: Methyl isocyanate (MIC) leaked from the Union Carbide pesticide plant at Bhopal.

questions.q: Joint Forest Management in India involves
options: Local communities and the forest department sharing management and benefits
questions.exp: JFM (1990) involves village committees in protecting forests in return for usufruct benefits.

questions.q: Ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays, is present in which layer of the atmosphere?
questions.exp: About 90% of atmospheric ozone lies in the stratosphere (15-35 km).

questions.q: The Earth Summit held at Rio de Janeiro in 1992 resulted in which of the following?
options: Convention on Biological Diversity and Agenda 21
questions.exp: The 1992 UN Conference on Environment and Development opened CBD and UNFCCC for signature and adopted Agenda 21.

questions.q: Which Act restricts diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes without central government approval?
questions.exp: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 regulates de-reservation of forests and use of forest land.

questions.q: Eutrophication of a lake is mainly caused by an excess of
questions.exp: Nutrient enrichment causes algal blooms; decay of algae depletes dissolved oxygen.

questions.q: Tsunamis are mostly caused by
questions.exp: Sudden vertical displacement of the sea floor during undersea earthquakes generates tsunami waves.

questions.q: Which organisation maintains the Red Data Book (Red List) of threatened species?
questions.exp: The International Union for Conservation of Nature maintains the IUCN Red List.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the ecological niche of an organism?
options: Its functional role and position in the ecosystem
The number of individuals in a population
The nutrients present in the soil
questions.exp: Habitat is the address; niche is the occupation or role of the species.

questions.q: In the food chain Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Hawk, which organism is the secondary consumer?
questions.exp: Grasshopper is the primary consumer; frog, which eats it, is the secondary consumer.

questions.q: The Indian Parliament enacted the Environment (Protection) Act in 1986 following which event?
questions.exp: The Bhopal gas leak (1984) of methyl isocyanate prompted the umbrella Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

questions.q: Fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum are formed from
options: Remains of ancient plants and animals buried and heated over millions of years
questions.exp: Burial under heat and pressure converts organic remains into coal, oil and gas.

questions.q: The National Green Tribunal was established in India in
questions.exp: The NGT Act, 2010 created a specialised body for speedy disposal of environmental cases.

questions.q: Which of the following contributes to sea-level rise due to global warming?
options: Thermal expansion of sea water and melting of land ice
Melting of floating sea ice only
questions.exp: Warmer water expands and melting glaciers/ice sheets add water to oceans.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a biotic component of an ecosystem?
questions.exp: Biotic components are living organisms - producers, consumers and decomposers.

questions.q: Which of the following is the process used in a nuclear power plant to generate energy?
questions.exp: Nuclear reactors split heavy nuclei such as uranium-235 to release energy.

questions.q: The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997, mainly aims at
options: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions of industrialised countries
Controlling trade in wild fauna and flora
Banning transboundary movement of hazardous wastes
questions.exp: The Kyoto Protocol set legally binding GHG reduction targets for developed countries.

questions.q: Carbon monoxide is harmful to humans because it
options: Combines with haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin
questions.exp: CO has far greater affinity for haemoglobin than oxygen, reducing oxygen transport.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Pyramid of numbers in a tree ecosystem is usually inverted.
Reason (R): A single large tree supports a large number of insects and other consumers.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: One producer (tree) supports many primary consumers, so the base is narrower than the next level.

questions.q: The Stockholm Conference of 1972 is notable because it
options: Was the first major UN conference on the human environment
questions.exp: It led to the creation of UNEP and the observance of World Environment Day on 5 June.

questions.q: The process by which plants release water vapour into the atmosphere is called
questions.exp: Transpiration through stomata returns water to the atmosphere in the water cycle.

questions.q: Which convention regulates the transboundary movement of hazardous wastes?
questions.exp: The Basel Convention (1989) controls the movement and disposal of hazardous wastes across borders.

questions.q: A solar photovoltaic cell converts
questions.exp: Photovoltaic cells (usually silicon) use the photoelectric effect to produce electricity from sunlight.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
questions.exp: Greenhouse gases absorb infrared radiation; molecular nitrogen does not.

questions.q: The scientific study of the relationship between living organisms and their physical environment is called
questions.exp: Ecology (term coined by Ernst Haeckel) studies organisms and their interactions with the environment.

questions.q: Which gas listed below has the highest Global Warming Potential per molecule over 100 years?
questions.exp: SF6 has a GWP of more than 20,000 times CO2.

questions.q: The Kanwar Lake (Kabartal) wetland, a Ramsar site, is located in which Bihar district?
questions.exp: Kabartal (Kanwar Jheel) in Begusarai was designated a Ramsar site in 2020.

questions.q: The major component of biogas is
questions.exp: Biogas, produced by anaerobic decomposition of organic matter, contains about 55-65% methane.

questions.q: PM2.5 in air quality measurement refers to particulate matter with diameter
questions.exp: PM2.5 particles are fine enough to enter the lungs and bloodstream.

questions.q: Project Tiger was launched in India in the year
questions.exp: Project Tiger started on 1 April 1973 from Jim Corbett National Park.

questions.q: Forests act as carbon sinks because they
options: Absorb CO2 during photosynthesis and store carbon in biomass
questions.exp: Trees fix atmospheric CO2 and store carbon in wood and soil.

questions.q: Which of the following is a perpetual (inexhaustible) resource?
questions.exp: Solar energy is available continuously and is not depleted by use; groundwater, forests and soil are renewable only if managed.

questions.q: Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) used as a cleaner vehicle fuel is mainly composed of
questions.exp: CNG is mostly methane, burning with lower particulate emissions than petrol or diesel.

questions.q: Narmada Bachao Andolan was led by
questions.exp: Medha Patkar led the movement against large dams on the Narmada, especially the Sardar Sarovar project.

questions.q: The Ramsar Convention, 1971, deals with the conservation of
questions.exp: Ramsar (Iran) Convention provides for wise use and conservation of wetlands.

questions.q: Noise level is measured in
questions.exp: The decibel (dB) is the unit of sound intensity level.

questions.q: The ozone hole is most pronounced over which region?
questions.exp: Extremely cold stratospheric clouds over Antarctica enable rapid ozone destruction in spring.

questions.q: Which of the following layers of the atmosphere contains most of the weather phenomena?
questions.exp: The troposphere, the lowest layer, contains most water vapour, clouds and weather.

questions.q: The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol aims to phase down
questions.exp: HFCs do not harm ozone but are strong greenhouse gases.

questions.q: Thermal pollution of rivers caused by power plants chiefly results in
options: Decrease in dissolved oxygen of water
questions.exp: Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen, harming aquatic life.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct set of the three levels of biodiversity?
questions.exp: Biodiversity is studied at genetic, species and ecosystem levels.

questions.q: The soil conservation method of ploughing along the contour lines of a slope helps to
options: Reduce soil erosion by slowing run-off
questions.exp: Contour ploughing creates barriers to run-off, retaining water and soil.

questions.q: A keystone species is one that
options: Is found only in one area
Has a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem relative to its abundance
questions.exp: Removal of keystone species such as sea otters or top predators changes ecosystem structure significantly.

questions.q: Which was the first biosphere reserve of India, established in 1986?
questions.exp: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was the first in India, covering parts of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.

questions.q: Pneumatophores or breathing roots are characteristic of which ecosystem?
questions.exp: Mangroves growing in waterlogged saline mud have pneumatophores for gas exchange.

questions.q: Valmiki Tiger Reserve, the only tiger reserve of Bihar, is located in which district?
questions.exp: Valmiki Tiger Reserve lies in West Champaran, bordering Nepal's Chitwan National Park.

questions.q: The Wildlife (Protection) Act of India was enacted in the year
questions.exp: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 provides for protection of wild animals, birds and plants.

questions.q: The movement 'Appiko' in the Western Ghats of Karnataka was aimed at
options: Saving trees from felling by embracing them
questions.exp: Appiko (Kannada for hugging) was launched in 1983 in Uttara Kannada by Pandurang Hegde.

questions.q: The maximum number of individuals of a species that the environment can sustain indefinitely is called
questions.exp: Carrying capacity (K) is the upper asymptote of the logistic growth curve.

questions.q: Excess exposure to UV-B radiation reaching the Earth's surface due to ozone depletion can cause
questions.exp: UV-B damages DNA and the lens of the eye.

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary pollutant?
questions.exp: Primary pollutants are emitted directly; ozone and PAN are formed by reactions in air.

questions.q: The pH of normal unpolluted rain water is approximately
questions.exp: CO2 dissolves in rain to form carbonic acid, making natural rain slightly acidic (pH about 5.6).

questions.q: The Brundtland Commission report 'Our Common Future' (1987) defined sustainable development as development that
options: Stops all use of natural resources
Meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs
questions.exp: This definition of sustainable development comes from the World Commission on Environment and Development.

questions.q: An orchid growing on the branch of a mango tree is an example of
questions.exp: The epiphytic orchid benefits (support, light) while the tree is neither harmed nor helped.

questions.q: The Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) is carried out
options: Before starting a development project to assess its likely environmental effects
questions.exp: EIA is a pre-project study to predict and mitigate environmental impacts.

questions.q: The type of disaster to which a cyclone belongs is
questions.exp: Cyclones originate in atmospheric conditions, unlike earthquakes and landslides.

questions.q: Species richness generally
options: Increases from the poles towards the equator
Increases from the equator to poles
Remains the same at all latitudes
questions.exp: Tropical regions have more stable climate and energy, supporting greater species diversity.

questions.q: The Biological Diversity Act of India was passed in
questions.exp: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 led to creation of the National Biodiversity Authority (Chennai).

questions.q: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was set up by
questions.exp: IPCC was established in 1988 by the United Nations Environment Programme and World Meteorological Organization.

questions.q: The Montreal Protocol (1987) was adopted to control the production and use of
questions.exp: The Montreal Protocol phases out substances such as CFCs and halons that deplete the ozone layer.

questions.q: A lichen is an example of which type of ecological interaction?
questions.exp: A lichen is an association of an alga (or cyanobacterium) and a fungus benefiting both.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the biodiversity hotspots found in India?
questions.exp: The Amazon basin is in South America; India has parts of Himalaya, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma and Sundaland hotspots.

questions.q: According to Lindeman's 10 per cent law, how much energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next?
questions.exp: Only about one-tenth of energy is passed to the next trophic level; the rest is lost as heat and respiration.
